curriculum.subject: Mathematical Activities
curriculum.outcomeText: appreciate measuring length using arbitrary units.

mission.title: appreciate measuring length using arbitrary units.

interactions.prompt: Mosi wants to know how long his pencil is. What can he use to measure it today?
interactions.feedback: Yes! Paper clips can help us measure length.
interactions.retryHint: Choose objects that can lie along the pencil.

interactions.prompt: Help the lion measure a storybook. Put 5 bottle tops from one end to the other.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap each of the five bottle-top spaces from left to right.
interactions.feedback: Great! The bottle tops touch in one line, so the book can be measured fairly.
interactions.retryHint: Start at one end. Put every bottle top next to the last one, with no gaps.

interactions.prompt: A desk is measured with cubes. Which row is ready to use?
choices: cubes touching from one end to the other
cubes piled on top of each other
interactions.answer: cubes touching from one end to the other
interactions.feedback: Well done! Units must touch in a straight row.
interactions.retryHint: Good measuring has no gaps and no piles.

interactions.prompt: Amina measures the class mat with 7 hand spans. Tap the label that tells her length.
interactions.feedback: Correct! Amina can say the mat is 7 hand spans long.
interactions.retryHint: Use the number and the thing Amina used to measure.

interactions.prompt: Match each job to a good measuring unit: a leaf, a crayon, and a table edge.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap an object, then tap its measuring unit.
interactions.feedback: Wonderful! Different everyday objects can help us measure length.
interactions.retryHint: Pick a small unit that can be placed in a line along each object.

interactions.prompt: Show what you know. Why do we measure a ribbon with paper clips?
choices: to find how long it is
interactions.answer: to find how long it is
interactions.feedback: You did it! Measuring helps us find how long things are in daily life.
interactions.retryHint: Think about what length tells us.
